outcome: Upper workspace management is simplified around the current Experiment
owner_impact: The current Experiment surface now uses one compact Experiments entry instead of Switch experiment wording; Professor opens Extension Requests directly with no intermediate Professor-tools screen; and Professor accounts can Promote to Showcase or Publish current revision directly beside the current Experiment. The Showcase browser remains available for browsing and removing curated entries. Arena and Experiment Source are unchanged.

next.text: The bounded #413 upper-workspace UI/UX cleanup round is complete. #273 remains a living evidence-driven UI/UX domain, with no automatic successor and no owner action required.

technical_evidence: The hidden legacy experiment select remains the internal compatibility/state source, while the visible current-Experiment surface exposes one Experiments library action.
The legacy Professor button now opens the existing Extension Requests inbox directly; Account remains the only workspace-utilities dialog view.
Desktop and mobile React Professor controls now point their dialog accessibility metadata at professor-extension-inbox rather than workspace-utilities.

Professor Showcase publication reuses the existing publication RPCs and save-before-publish semantics, but the action is mounted beside the current Experiment with Promote to Showcase, Publish current revision, In Showcase and conflict states.
The Showcase browser retains curated-entry browsing, opening, removal and private-copy behavior; no publication or authorization contract changed.
Arena, simulation controls, Experiment Source, revision/autosave semantics, sharing, collections, capability-request data, scientific runtime, connectors, CI/CD and project workflow are unchanged.
Focused #413 regression coverage locks the simplified Experiment entry, one-step Professor navigation and direct Showcase curation path.

The responsive production smoke now locks the approved visible Experiment-library label as Experiments while retaining all existing identity, hidden-select, persistence, hierarchy and touch-target assertions.
